comments.story: Kimi K3, and what we can still learn from the pelican benchmark
comments.why: On-the-ground reporting in China on how restricted GPUs get sold and carried.
comments.text: Gamers Nexus has a good video where his team travelled to China and did some actual investigative journalism: [VIDEO] Firstly, the export-restricted GB202s (e.g. 5090, RTX 6000 Pro Blackwell) are fabled in TSMC, and then packaged/made in... China before they supposedly have to be sold out (by US law; but not by Chinese law). You can immediately see the problem there. Secondly, despite the supposed 'crackdowns' and et al, NVIDIA and their channel partners pretty much will sell to anyone in countries like Singapore without any questions. Third, there's human "smugglers" who just physically carry em on trips, and Chinese customs is obviously not going to care about the US's laws on Chinese soil.

comments.why: Shows export controls raise GPU prices in China without stopping acquisition.
comments.text: The GamersNexus documentary ( [VIDEO] ) on the semi-underground GPU trade in China, while a little amateurish in terms of depth and general atmosphere, is an interesting watch and may answer some of your questions. Basically, those export controls make GPUs more expensive for affected parties in China, but don't effectively stop them from being acquired or used over there.
